plan: Classify the observed pattern and confidence
Identify visibility gaps and next evidence sources

EVID-001.claim: A fully automated cluster queried the vulnerable endpoint at scale.

EVID-002.claim: The automated activity escalated month over month.

EVID-003.claim: HTTP 200 responses indicate a conservative population potentially disclosed.

facts.caveat: Status alone does not prove response body or PII delivery.

EVID-004.claim: The activity spans the complete observed window and all logged sites.

assessment:
Classification: HIGH confidence of automated exploitation compatible with IDOR; MEDIUM confidence of PII disclosure.

Five automated sources generated 61,961 requests with only 4 tokens and touched 10,181 distinct invoices [EVID-001]. The monthly progression was 2025-10: 1,488, 2025-11: 15,120, 2025-12: 45,353 [EVID-002]. There were 44,868 HTTP 200 responses spanning 10,173 invoices; this is a conservative potential-exposure set, not proof that response bodies contained PII [EVID-003]. The observed activity spans the entire three-month window and all four sites [EVID-004].

Immediate actions: disable object access based solely on invoice_id; enforce server-side subject-to-object authorization; revoke the four implicated tokens; preserve CDN/WAF, application, identity and database logs; notify Legal/Privacy; and hunt for the five source fingerprints across the wider estate. Strategic actions: centralized authorization, negative access-control tests in CI, object-access audit trails, rate controls and anomaly alerts.
